summary: Flex Logistics is a privately held 3PL operating 13 facilities (~3 million sq ft, 9 food-grade) across four U.S. regions, with its Eastern-region food-grade and cross-dock hub at 121 Ridge Road in Jamesburg, NJ, where it serves grocery, CPG, retail/DSD and e-commerce shippers. The company is the product of a roll-up: Partners Warehouse (Chicago-area, joined 2022) and PSS Distribution Services (Northeast, founded 1983, acquired December 2024 and headquartered in Jamesburg). Demand intake is a web quote form plus a single toll-free sales line, order and inventory execution runs on a Softeon WMS behind an older WebSynapse customer portal, and current Jamesburg hiring (Transportation Manager, Inventory Control Specialist) points at dispatch, routing and inventory-accuracy workload.

facts.fact: Operates 13 facilities totaling 3 million sq ft, of which 9 are food-grade warehouses, organized in Western, Central, Eastern and Southwestern regions.
Ridge Warehouse at 121 Ridge Rd, Jamesburg, NJ 08831 is described as food-grade with AIB compliance, full cross-docking, an on-site rail siding, and 10,000 sq ft of temperature-controlled storage.

Jamesburg location services list: warehousing and inventory management, pick & pack fulfillment, e-commerce fulfillment, cross-docking & transloading, transportation & freight brokerage; facility capabilities cite 'Advanced WMS and EDI integrations'.

Inbound demand is captured through a web quote form (service-type checkboxes plus a required 'Primary Service Location' state dropdown, reCAPTCHA v2) and a single sales channel - 800-350-4567 and sales@flexlogistics.com - for all regions.
Customers log into a portal at http://www.flexwebportal.com:8080/WebSynapse/ (plain HTTP, port 8080).

Softeon case study states Flex 'relied on manual spreadsheets and outdated systems to track inventory and lot codes' before implementing Softeon WMS, and now uses voice picking, wave picking, integrated EDI and cycle counts; headquarters listed as Jamesburg, New Jersey.

Company LinkedIn lists 201-500 employees, headquarters in Eastvale, CA, and about 51 members on LinkedIn; specialties include warehousing and distribution, e-commerce, value-added services, pick and pack, food grade, labeling, kitting and transloading.

Brand history: Partners Warehouse (founded 1989, Chicago area) joined Flex in 2022; PSS Distribution Services (founded 1983, Northeast corridor) joined in 2024; the site's structured data lists foundingDate 1984 and the About page claims 'over 25 years' of 3PL experience.
Directory record shows business hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, closed Saturday and Sunday, at 121 Ridge Rd, Jamesburg, phone 732-992-1300.
Customer-review aggregate for the Jamesburg address shows a 2.8 rating; of 147 reviews, 65 are 1-star and 50 are 5-star.
Birdeye lists the same Jamesburg business as 2.8 stars from 175 reviews with weekday hours 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. and weekend closure, and the profile is unclaimed by the business.

Press-release archive documents recurring customer recognition: Bumble Bee Foods warehouse-of-the-year awards (2018, 2019, 2023), Barilla America warehouse-of-the-year/quarter awards, and a World Finer Foods service recognition.

operations_signals: No online booking or self-scheduling: the only published paths are the web quote form, the 800-350-4567 line, or sales@flexlogistics.com, so every new engagement starts with a human qualification and estimating step (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).

The quote form asks only for service interest, state, contact details and a free-text message - no volume, SKU count, temperature regime or inbound/outbound cadence - so scoping data has to be gathered manually afterward (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).

Published hours for the Jamesburg address are 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. Monday-Friday with weekends closed; no after-hours or 24/7 coverage is stated on the website (https://www.chamberofcommerce.com/business-directory/new-jersey/jamesburg/warehouse/10717163-pss-distribution-services).

The footprint is multi-site and multi-region (13 facilities, 4 regions) yet all inquiries route to one toll-free number and one email, so directing a lead to the right facility and CSR is manual (https://flexlogistics.com/facilities).

Customer-facing system access is a legacy WebSynapse portal over plain HTTP on port 8080 rather than a modern API or SSO, which typically means EDI/CSV/email exchange and manual lookups for status requests (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).

The service model is explicitly exception-heavy - cross-docking, transloading, kitting, labeling, retail compliance, returns/reverse logistics and direct-to-store delivery all require per-order coordination (https://flexlogistics.com/solutions).
hiring_signals: Transportation Manager, Jamesburg, NJ - on-site, full-time, $70k-$80k, posted about 12 hours before this review: owns routing, scheduling and dispatching, customer-service management, carrier relationships, service-issue resolution and KPI tracking (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/transportation-manager-at-flex-logistics-4488635615).

Inventory Control Specialist, Jamesburg, NJ - entry level, full-time, posted the same day, pointing at cycle-count and inventory-accuracy workload in the DC (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/inventory-control-specialist-at-flex-logistics-4487873392).

Only 2 roles were live on the company's LinkedIn jobs page at review time, both in Jamesburg, so hiring is concentrated at the NJ hub rather than corporate functions (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/flex-logistics-jobs-worldwide?f_C=1379186).

The careers page hosts no postings itself and instead points applicants to LinkedIn, Indeed and ZipRecruiter, a decentralized intake that is hard to keep synchronized (https://flexlogistics.com/careers).
review_themes: Overall sentiment for the Jamesburg address is polarized and negative-leaning: 2.8 stars, with 65 of 147 ratings at 1 star against 50 at 5 stars (https://www.chamberofcommerce.com/business-directory/new-jersey/jamesburg/warehouse/10717163-pss-distribution-services).

Dominant complaint theme is dock wait time: one reviewer describes waiting about six hours for a single pallet and calls it among the worst places in New Jersey to pick up, while another treats an hour in and out as a good outcome (https://www.chamberofcommerce.com/business-directory/new-jersey/jamesburg/warehouse/10717163-pss-distribution-services).

Second recurring theme is how counter/dock staff treat drivers, with a review describing staff as rude (https://www.chamberofcommerce.com/business-directory/new-jersey/jamesburg/warehouse/10717163-pss-distribution-services).

Positive reviews are short and service-oriented, crediting 'professional and quality service' and helpful, prompt customer-service staff (https://www.chamberofcommerce.com/business-directory/new-jersey/jamesburg/warehouse/10717163-pss-distribution-services; https://flexlogistics.com/industries).

The aggregation shows the review profile as not claimed by the business owner, so review responses and listing updates appear unmanaged (https://reviews.birdeye.com/pss-distribution-services-166517514477152).
tech_footprint: Warehouse management: Softeon WMS with voice picking, wave picking, lot and lock-code traceability, cycle counts and integrated EDI; the vendor publishes Flex as a named case study (https://www.softeon.com/case-study/flex-logistics/).
Customer portal: WebSynapse login at http://www.flexwebportal.com:8080/WebSynapse/, unencrypted HTTP on a non-standard port (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).

Website stack: Craft CMS with the Freeform plugin for quote and newsletter forms, reCAPTCHA v2, CookieYes consent banner, Google Tag Manager plus GA4, a HubSpot tracking script, and Elfsight embedded widgets; site credited to Breakout Studio (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).
No live chat, chatbot, scheduling widget or self-service quote tool appears on the home, contact, solutions or careers pages (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).

Content marketing is active: nine-plus insight articles published July-October 2026 on 3PL topics (cross-docking, shelf life, packaging costs, peak-season surges), each feeding the quote form (https://flexlogistics.com/news).
Email addresses are Cloudflare-obfuscated on the contact page, and every region shares one sales email and one toll-free number (https://flexlogistics.com/contact).
growth_signals: Roll-up trajectory: Partners Warehouse joined the Flex family in 2022 (six Chicago-area locations) and PSS Distribution Services joined in 2024, taking the network to 13 facilities and about 3 million sq ft (https://flexlogistics.com/about; https://flexlogistics.com/facilities).

The PSS acquisition closed December 12, 2024, with PSS described as a Jamesburg-headquartered Northeast 3PL serving food, grocery, retail, food service, DSD and e-commerce (directory record seen in search: https://mergr.com/transaction/flex-logistics-acquires-pss-distribution-services).

New city landing pages were added through mid-2026 for Ontario CA, Elwood IL, Jamesburg NJ and Hutchins TX, indicating an active geographic marketing push (https://flexlogistics.com/sitemaps-1-section-pages-1-sitemap.xml).

The facility roster shows newer NJ capacity - Mansfield 351,000 sq ft with 98 doors, Westampton 300,000 sq ft with 17,500 rack positions - alongside the older Ridge Road site, consistent with Northeast expansion (https://flexlogistics.com/facilities).

Long-running recognition from CPG shippers (Bumble Bee, Barilla, World Finer Foods) suggests stable anchor accounts that bring seasonal and promotional volume swings (https://www.pssdistribution.com/press-releases/).

Both open Jamesburg roles were posted simultaneously, indicating near-term staffing pressure at the NJ hub rather than routine backfill (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/flex-logistics-jobs-worldwide?f_C=1379186).
decision_maker: Unknown - flexlogistics.com has no leadership or team page. The company's own LinkedIn job posting names Gladys Guzman, Human Resources Director - Flex Logistics, as the posting contact (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/inventory-control-specialist-at-flex-logistics-4487873392). A third-party contact database (RocketReach) lists Stefan Freeman as CEO, but that is not confirmed on any company-owned page.

inferences.inference: Dock appointment scheduling and driver check-in at Jamesburg are manual and are a visible service-quality bottleneck.
inferences.reasoning: Public reviews concentrate on multi-hour driver waits and counter-staff friction at the 121 Ridge Rd address, and the company is simultaneously hiring a Transportation Manager whose scope covers routing, scheduling, dispatching and service-issue resolution - a pattern consistent with unautomated appointment and flow control rather than pure capacity shortage.

inferences.inference: Quote-to-onboarding is a labor-intensive, human-driven process with slow turnaround.
inferences.reasoning: The form collects only service type, state and free text (no volumes, SKUs, temperature class or cadence), there is no instant pricing, and one toll-free line plus one sales inbox serve 13 facilities across four regions; every quote therefore requires manual discovery, site selection and pricing before a proposal exists.

inferences.inference: The integration of PSS and Partners Warehouse left duplicated systems and inconsistent processes across sites.
inferences.reasoning: The company still runs multiple brand narratives (Flex plus Partners Warehouse plus PSS, with PSS's separate website and press-release archive), the acquisition closed only in December 2024, and the customer portal is a legacy HTTP WebSynapse endpoint while the WMS underneath is Softeon - typical of partially consolidated post-merger IT.

inferences.inference: EDI and lot-code exceptions are handled by clerical staff rather than automated workflows.
inferences.reasoning: The Softeon case study describes EDI plus 'automated clerical tools' as the fix for earlier spreadsheet-based lot tracking and recounts, and the company is recruiting an entry-level inventory control specialist at the same site, suggesting ongoing manual reconciliation and exception chasing.

inferences.inference: Reputation management is effectively unowned, which likely suppresses inbound lead quality.
inferences.reasoning: The review profile for the main Jamesburg address is unclaimed with a 2.8 average and a large 1-star block, and the company website shows no review content, rating display or response mechanism.

inferences.inference: After-hours and weekend coverage is handled informally rather than through a documented process.
inferences.reasoning: Published hours stop at 4:00 p.m. weekdays with weekends closed and no 24/7 or on-call language on the site, yet retail/DSD clients commonly need evening and weekend exception handling to hit compliance windows.

data_gaps: Indeed company pages and reviews and Glassdoor reviews were blocked by login walls or CAPTCHA, so employee-sentiment themes could not be collected.
The BBB business profile returned HTTP 403, so accreditation status, complaint counts and BBB letter rating are unverified beyond a search snippet.
Review text could only be sampled (five excerpts) because aggregator pages paginate behind scripts; no systematic coding of all ~150 reviews was possible.
No headcount by site, revenue, tonnage, SKU counts or appointment volumes are published; LinkedIn's 201-500 band and 51 members on LinkedIn are the only size indicators found.
CEO and ownership confirmation is missing from company-owned sources; the RocketReach management listing (Stefan Freeman as CEO) is third-party and unverified.
ZipRecruiter and Indeed postings could not be opened (403/login), so only LinkedIn listings were reviewed and the true count of open roles may exceed two.
No information on current WMS version, TMS provider, EDI transaction volumes, telephony/phone system, or whether any AI or automation tooling is already in use.
No local news coverage of the Jamesburg facility specifically was found; growth evidence rests on the company site, the Softeon case study and M&A/press-release directories.
